title: CampusOS Academic Guidelines and Student Code (MVP Policy Example)
content: These academic guidelines govern student enrollment, course registration, grading policies, and scholastic integrity at CampusOS.

title: CampusOS Academic Guidelines and Student Code (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Course Enrollment:
   - Students register for required core courses and electives offered by their respective academic departments at the beginning of each semester.
   - Course listings specify course codes, department affiliations, credit units, prerequisites, and assigned faculty instructors.
2. Add/Drop Period:
   - Students may adjust course schedules during the designated add/drop registration window without academic penalty.
3. Credit Load:
   - Full-time students must maintain the prescribed minimum credit hours per semester according to their program curriculum.

title: CampusOS Academic Guidelines and Student Code (MVP Policy Example)
content:
- Performance evaluation includes continuous assessments, mid-term examinations, and final semester evaluations.
- Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is computed based on weighted credit grades across all completed academic semesters.
- Students must maintain satisfactory academic standing according to departmental standards.

title: CampusOS Academic Guidelines and Student Code (MVP Policy Example)
section: Scholastic Honesty and Code of Conduct
content:
- Plagiarism, unauthorized examination collaboration, and fraudulent submission of academic work are serious violations.
- Violations are subject to disciplinary review and penalties ranging from assignment failure to course debarment.

title: CampusOS Attendance Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: Regular attendance in scheduled academic sessions is essential for student learning and academic performance across all departments.

title: CampusOS Attendance Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Minimum Requirement: Students are required to maintain a minimum attendance threshold of 75% in each registered course to be eligible for end-semester examinations.
2. Attendance Status Classification:
   - Good Standing: Attendance percentage at or above 75%.
   - Warning Status: Attendance percentage between 65% and 74%.
   - Critical Status: Attendance percentage below 65%.
3. Debarment: Students falling below 75% without authorized condonation may be debarred from taking final examinations.

title: CampusOS Attendance Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
- Faculty members record attendance for each course session through the CampusOS Attendance module.
- Students can view their attendance logs, current percentage, and required classes needed to reach 75% on their student dashboard.
- Attendance records cannot be marked or modified directly by students.

title: CampusOS Attendance Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: - In exceptional circumstances such as documented illness or university-approved event participation, attendance condonation may be granted down to 65% upon timely submission of official medical or event certificates to the department.

title: CampusOS CampusFix Issue Reporting Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: CampusFix is the centralized university complaint and facility issue resolution system designed to maintain campus infrastructure and student amenities.

title: CampusOS CampusFix Issue Reporting Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Submission: Students and campus members can lodge maintenance and facility complaints through the CampusFix portal on the CampusOS dashboard.
2. Complaint Categories:
   - Maintenance: Structural repairs, plumbing, furniture, and general campus facilities.
   - Electrical: Lighting, power outlets, circuit breakers, and laboratory power fixtures.
   - IT: Wi-Fi connectivity, lab workstations, network access points, and system errors.
   - Other: General campus amenities and custodial services.
3. Priority Levels:
   - Issues can be designated with urgency levels: Low, Medium, High, or Urgent.

title: CampusOS CampusFix Issue Reporting Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
- Open: The complaint has been registered and is pending initial review by campus facility staff.
- In Progress: A maintenance technician or IT personnel has been assigned and work is actively underway.
- Resolved: Corrective actions have been completed and verified.
- Status Notifications: The reporting user receives real-time notifications in their CampusOS Notification Center whenever the complaint status transitions.

title: CampusOS Events and Clubs Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: Campus events and student organizations foster community engagement, leadership development, and extracurricular learning.

title: CampusOS Events and Clubs Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Browsing Events: Upcoming workshops, hackathons, guest lectures, and cultural fests are cataloged in the CampusOS Events section.
2. Registering:
   - Any registered student can sign up for an active event with available seats.
   - Upon successful registration, the student receives an event confirmation and ticket record.
   - If unable to attend, students can unregister prior to the event start time to free up seating.
3. Event Creation: Authorized faculty and club administrators can create and manage event details, capacity, venue, and timings.

title: CampusOS Events and Clubs Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Membership:
   - Students may explore technical societies, arts collectives, and student clubs via the Clubs directory.
   - Joining a club adds the student to the active membership roster.
   - A student can leave a club at any time from their club membership dashboard.
2. Club Governance:
   - Official club creation requires authorization from campus administration or faculty advisors.
   - All student members are expected to uphold the university student code of conduct during club operations.

title: CampusOS Internship and Career Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: The CampusOS Internship & Career module connects undergraduate and graduate students with verified professional opportunities and industrial training.

title: CampusOS Internship and Career Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content:
1. Eligibility: Students in eligible academic terms with active student status can explore and apply for internship postings.
2. Skill Matching System:
   - Internship listings define required technical and professional skills (such as Python, SQL, React, Machine Learning, Fastapi).
   - CampusOS computes an explainable skill match percentage comparing the student's acquired skills with the posting requirements.
   - Students can review their matching skills and missing skills before applying.
3. Application Process:
   - Applications are submitted through the CampusOS Internship portal.
   - Applicants provide their portfolio link, resume URL, and statement of interest.
   - Duplicate applications for the same opening are strictly prohibited.
   - Students can monitor their application history and status from the My Applications dashboard.

title: CampusOS Internship and Career Policy (MVP Policy Example)
content: - Students who receive an official internship offer must notify the Career and Placement cell and verify that work hours do not conflict with mandatory class schedules.
